cues.zh: 五年前，我为 Computerphile 频道做了一个视频
cues.en: Five years ago, I made a video for a channel called Computerphile

cues.zh: 讲为什么电子投票是个坏主意。
cues.en: about why electronic voting is a bad idea.

cues.zh: 我偶尔还会收到邮件问：
cues.en: And I still get emails, occasionally, asking:

cues.zh: 到现在情况肯定变了吧？
cues.en: things must have changed by now, right?

cues.zh: 有个新想法，也许会有帮助。
cues.en: There’s this new idea, and maybe it’ll help.

cues.zh: 电子投票肯定快实现了吧？
cues.en: Surely electronic voting is just around the corner?

cues.zh: 不。
cues.en: No.

cues.zh: 不，真的没有。
cues.en: No, it’s really not.

cues.zh: 下面说说为什么电子投票仍然是个坏主意。
cues.en: Here is why electronic voting is still a bad idea.

cues.zh: 选举有一些非常特殊的要求。
cues.en: Elections have some very unusual requirements.

cues.zh: 有两个关键特性几乎是相互对立的：
cues.en: There are two key features that are almost opposed to each other:

cues.zh: 匿名性和信任。
cues.en: anonymity and trust.

cues.zh: 首先，你的投票应该完全匿名。
cues.en: So first, your vote should be completely anonymous.

cues.zh: 任何人都不应该能查出你投给了谁，
cues.en: There should be no way that anyone can find out who you voted for,

cues.zh: 即使所有票都统计完之后也不行。
cues.en: even after everything’s been counted.

cues.zh: 这样，没人能贿赂或威胁你按特定方式投票。
cues.en: That way, no-one can bribe you or threaten you to vote a particular way.

cues.zh: 在英国，如果你在选票上做标记的方式可能暴露你的身份，
cues.en: In the UK, if you mark your ballot in a way that could potentially identify you,

cues.zh: 比如你签了名，那张选票就不算数。
cues.en: so if you sign it, for example, then that ballot is not counted.

cues.zh: 这就是为什么选举官员担心有人会
cues.en: This is why election officials are worried about people taking selfies

cues.zh: 和填好的选票一起自拍：
cues.en: with their completed ballots:

cues.zh: 因为事后你不应该能证明自己投给了谁。
cues.en: because you should not be able to prove how you voted afterwards.

cues.zh: 否则，就会出现像“蓝方选民优惠10美元！”这样的攻击，
cues.en: Otherwise, you can have attacks like “$10 off for blue voters!”

cues.zh: 或者“这个聚会只准黄方选民入场！”
cues.en: or “Entry to this party only for yellow voters!”

cues.zh: 或者“投红色，不然你会后悔的。”
cues.en: or “vote red or you’ll regret it.”

cues.zh: 投票必须匿名。
cues.en: Votes have to be anonymous.

cues.zh: 第二项要求是绝对、透明的信任。
cues.en: The second requirement is absolute, transparent trust.

cues.zh: 系统当然要确保你的选票被安全、准确地统计。
cues.en: The system needs to make sure that your vote is securely and accurately counted, sure.

cues.zh: 但它也必须让所有人——无论懂不懂技术——都清楚，
cues.en: But it also needs to be obvious to everyone, no matter their technical knowledge,

cues.zh: 这套系统值得信任。
cues.en: that the system can be trusted.

cues.zh: 所以如果用纸质选票，就把选票放进密封箱里
cues.en: So if you’re using paper, you place your ballot in a sealed box

cues.zh: 直到选举中所有利益相关方
cues.en: that doesn’t get unsealed until everyone with a stake in the election

cues.zh: 都有代表在场，才会打开。
cues.en: has someone representing them in the room.

cues.zh: 守护它的人应该始终来自不止一方，或者至少
cues.en: There should always be people from more than one side guarding it, or at the very least,

cues.zh: 要有人见证运输时使用了防篡改封条。
cues.en: witnessing that there's a tamper-proof seal being used for transport.

cues.zh: 选民需要能够相信自己的选票会被计入
cues.en: Voters need to be able to trust that their vote will be counted

cues.zh: 尽管他们再也见不到它，也无法追溯到他们本人。
cues.en: even though they’ll never see it again and it can’t be traced back to them.

cues.zh: 任何时候都不能把信任寄托在单个人身上。
cues.en: And at no point is a single person put in a position of trust.

cues.zh: 人可能腐败、受威胁、无能，或者三者同时具备。
cues.en: People can be corrupt, or threatened, or incompetent, or all three at the same time.

cues.zh: 当然，实体投票并不完美。
cues.en: Now, physical voting is not perfect.

cues.zh: 它可能被攻击，也确实被攻击过。
cues.en: It can be attacked, it has been attacked.

cues.zh: 英国自己的纸质系统也并未完美满足这两项要求，
cues.en: The UK’s own paper system doesn’t fulfil both of those requirements perfectly,

cues.zh: 如果法院下令，是可以从选票中识别出选民的，
cues.en: it is possible to identify voters from their ballots if a court orders it,

cues.zh: 而且也有传闻说，在法律之外也发生过这种事。
cues.en: and there are stories about that being done outside the law too.

cues.zh: 但关键不在于纸质投票是完美的：它并不是。
cues.en: But the key point is not that paper voting is perfect: it isn’t.

cues.zh: 但对它的攻击很难规模化。
cues.en: But attacks against it don’t scale well.

cues.zh: 实体投票已有几百年历史。
cues.en: Physical voting is centuries old.

cues.zh: 在这段时间里，几乎所有能想到的舞弊手段都被试过了，
cues.en: And in that time almost every conceivable fraud on the system has been tried,

cues.zh: 而防御手段也被找到了。
cues.en: and defences have been found.

cues.zh: 你需要改动的实体选票越多，
cues.en: The more physical votes you need to change,

cues.zh: 你需要影响的人就越多，
cues.en: the more people you need to influence,

cues.zh: 花费的时间和金钱就越多，
cues.en: the more time and money it takes,

cues.zh: 你那个小阴谋就越不可能保持秘密。
cues.en: and the less likely it is that your little conspiracy will stay secret.

cues.zh: 在英国选举中，全国有数百个投票站，
cues.en: In a UK election, there are hundreds of polling stations across the country,

cues.zh: 工作人员由几十名雇员和数千名志愿者组成。
cues.en: with staff made up of scores of employees and thousands of volunteers.

cues.zh: 想要改动足够多的选票、
cues.en: The job of changing a significant number of votes,

cues.zh: 足以左右选举结果，会变得非常非常困难。
cues.en: enough to sway an election, becomes very, very difficult.

cues.zh: 有人尝试过，有些人被定罪了，
cues.en: People have attempted it, some people have been convicted,

cues.zh: 少数人可能在一定程度上逃脱了惩罚。
cues.en: a few have probably gotten away with it on some scale.

cues.zh: “Granny farming”（养老院拉票）是不法分子用的说法
cues.en: “Granny farming” is the term that shady operatives use

cues.zh: 指挨个跑遍养老院
cues.en: for going round all the retirement homes

cues.zh: 让易受影响的老人签署委托投票书，
cues.en: and getting vulnerable elderly people to sign a proxy vote,

cues.zh: 也就是一份文件，写明可由别人代他们投票。
cues.en: a paper saying that someone else can vote on their behalf.

cues.zh: 是的，小规模下这确实行得通。
cues.en: And yeah, on a small scale, that has worked.

cues.zh: 但一旦开始扩大这种攻击规模
cues.en: But once you start scaling up that attack

cues.zh: 就会变得极其困难和耗时
cues.en: it becomes extremely difficult and time-consuming

cues.zh: 而且你很可能会被发现。
cues.en: and the chances are you’re going to get found out.

cues.zh: 电子投票就不是这样。
cues.en: With electronic voting, that’s not the case.

cues.zh: 首先，我们来说说电子投票机。
cues.en: So first, let’s talk about electronic voting machines.

cues.zh: 这种投票站里有一台电脑：
cues.en: That’s where there’s a computer at the polling station:

cues.zh: 选民仍然会走进投票亭，
cues.en: so voters still go into a booth,

cues.zh: 只不过他们按的是按钮，或在触摸屏上点选，
cues.en: it’s just that they are pushing buttons, or tapping things on a touchscreen,

cues.zh: 而不是在纸上写。
cues.en: not writing on paper.

cues.zh: 第一个问题：信任软件和硬件。
cues.en: Problem number one: trusting the software and the hardware.

cues.zh: 理论上，我们的投票计算机可能运行的是开源软件
cues.en: In theory, our voting computer could be running open source software

cues.zh: 任何人都能查看并检查源代码。
cues.en: where anyone can see and check the source code.

cues.zh: 但实际上，这并不会发生：
cues.en: In practice, that doesn’t happen:

cues.zh: 它很可能是闭源的，
cues.en: it’s probably going to be closed source,

cues.zh: 很可能是从一个容易被攻破的U盘里加载的，
cues.en: it's probably going to be loaded off an easily-compromised USB stick,

cues.zh: 装在一台无人看管的计算机上
cues.en: on a computer that’s been sitting unguarded

cues.zh: 有时还只是莫名其妙地闲置连着互联网，一放就是好几年。
cues.en: and sometimes just idly and inexplicably connected to the internet for years.

cues.zh: 而这些系统只有在真正举行选举时，才会接受一次全面测试。
cues.en: And those systems only ever get a full-scale test when an election actually takes place.

cues.zh: 仅这一点就足以让电子投票永远不该被采用。
cues.en: That in itself should be enough to stop electronic voting ever being a thing.

cues.zh: 但是，好吧，假设我们真的，神奇地，
cues.en: But, okay, let’s say that we do, magically,

cues.zh: 拥有了尽可能最稳定、最安全的开源软件。
cues.en: have the most stable, secure, open source software possible.

cues.zh: 选民如何知道并相信正确的软件确实已安装
cues.en: How does a voter know and trust that the correct software is actually installed

cues.zh: 在他们正在使用的机器上？
cues.en: on the machine they’re using?

cues.zh: 也许我们可以用某种校验和，或者其他系统
cues.en: Maybe we could use some sort of checksum or some other system

cues.zh: 来确保投票正常运行。
cues.en: to make sure the voting is running correctly.

cues.zh: 但那样只是把问题转移了，
cues.en: But then you’re just moving the problem,

cues.zh: 现在你得信任这个校验和没有被伪造。
cues.en: now you have to trust that checksum hasn’t been forged.

cues.zh: 而且几乎没有选民会真正理解那个校验到底意味着什么，
cues.en: And almost no voters actually will understand what that check even means,

cues.zh: 或者为什么他们该信任它。
cues.en: or why they should trust it.

cues.zh: 在美国，投票机每年都会定期接受测试……
cues.en: In the United States, voting machines are regularly tested every year...

cues.zh: 在 DEFCON 的 Voting Village，这是全球最大的黑客大会之一。
cues.en: at the Voting Village at DEFCON, one of the world's largest hacker conventions.

cues.zh: 这不是官方活动。
cues.en: It's not an official thing.

cues.zh: 那里的黑客已经成功篡改过存储的投票统计，
cues.en: Hackers there have managed to alter the stored vote tallies,

cues.zh: 改变展示给选民的选票，还有一次，
cues.en: change the ballots displayed to voters, and in one case,

cues.zh: 让一台机器运行起了电子游戏 Doom。
cues.en: have got a machine to run the video game Doom.

cues.zh: 想象一下，如果投票亭里不是机器，而只是一个人，
cues.en: Imagine if, instead of a machine, there was just a person in the voting booth,

cues.zh: 你得把票小声说给他们听，而他们保证，哦，是的，
cues.en: and you had to whisper your vote to them, and they promised, oh, yes,

cues.zh: 你完全可以信任他们会准确记录你的投票，
cues.en: you can absolutely trust them to accurately record your vote

cues.zh: 并把它转交给负责计票的人。
cues.en: and pass it on to the people who are doing the count.

cues.zh: 不，你看不到他们是怎么记、记在哪儿，
cues.en: No, you can’t see how or where they’re writing it down,

cues.zh: 你也没法真的打电话查他们在哪、在干什么，
cues.en: you can’t actually call and find out where they are or what they're doing,

cues.zh: 但他们拍胸脯保证。
cues.en: but they absolutely promise.

cues.zh: 电子投票机基本就是这样。
cues.en: That’s basically what’s happening with an electronic voting machine.

cues.zh: 你面对的只是一个东西，它说：相信我。
cues.en: You just have something that says: trust me.

cues.zh: 我已经统计了你的票，而且绝对没被动过手脚。
cues.en: I’ve counted your vote and I have absolutely not been compromised.

cues.zh: 真的。
cues.en: Honest.

cues.zh: 第二个问题是选票在运输途中。
cues.en: Problem number two is votes in transit.

cues.zh: 你怎么把选票从机器里弄出来，送到中央计票点？
cues.en: How do you get the votes off that machine to the central counting place?

cues.zh: 有三种可能的方式。
cues.en: There are three possible ways.

cues.zh: 第一，把所有投票机直接运到计票点。
cues.en: One, you could take all the voting machines to the count.

cues.zh: 你可以把它们全部封好，然后实体运输
cues.en: You could seal them all up, and transport them physically

cues.zh: 从投票地点运到计票地点。
cues.en: from where the voting took place to where the counting takes place.

cues.zh: 没人这么做。
cues.en: No one does that.

cues.zh: 所以，你可以把每台机器上的所有结果下载到 U 盘里，然后带走 U 盘。
cues.en: So, you could download all the results from each machine onto a USB stick and take that.

cues.zh: 一点障眼法，你就能得到一套完全不同的结果。
cues.en: One bit of sleight-of-hand and you’ve got a completely different set of results.

cues.zh: 如果你打算提出某个系统，让结果经过校验和并被信任：
cues.en: If you’re about to propose some system where the results are checksummed and trusted:

cues.zh: 请用普通选民能理解、并会本能信任的方式向他们解释这一点。
cues.en: please explain that to the average voter in a way they can understand and implicitly trust.

cues.zh: 好吧，那也许我们可以通过互联网以电子方式传输选票。
cues.en: Okay, so, maybe we could transmit the votes electronically over the internet.

cues.zh: 这……有点过于乐观了。
cues.en: Which is… optimistic.

cues.zh: 中间人攻击如今更难实施了，
cues.en: Man-in-the-middle attacks are more difficult now,

cues.zh: 但并非不可能，
cues.en: but they’re not impossible,

cues.zh: 尤其是当你无法信任两端软件的时候。
cues.en: particularly if you can’t trust the software on either end.

cues.zh: 而现在你还把投票机直接连到互联网上。
cues.en: And now you’re connecting the voting machines directly to the internet.

cues.zh: 还是故意的。
cues.en: Deliberately.

cues.zh: 这就引出了第三个问题：中央计票服务器。
cues.en: Which brings us to problem number three: the central counting server.

cues.zh: 在整个流程的最后，会有一台服务器
cues.en: Right at the end of the process there is the server

cues.zh: 负责统计选票并给出最终计数。
cues.en: that tallies the votes and gives the final count.

cues.zh: 它存在完全相同的信任与验证问题
cues.en: Which has all the same problems with trust and verification

cues.zh: 就像单台投票机那样，
cues.en: as the individual voting machines,

cues.zh: 但现在只有少数人能看到那台计算机。
cues.en: but now only a few people can even see that computer.

cues.zh: 电子计票机也是如此：
cues.en: That’s also true about electronic counting machines:

cues.zh: 它们接收成叠的纸质选票并返回总计结果。
cues.en: ones that take stacks of paper ballots and return totals.

cues.zh: 你怎么能相信它们没有悄悄改动某些选票？
cues.en: How do you trust they aren’t quietly changing some votes?

cues.zh: 我们生活在一个 Volkswagen 得以逍遥法外的世界里
cues.en: We live in a world where Volkswagen got away with

cues.zh: 他们专门设计汽车，多年来在排放测试中作弊。
cues.en: specifically designing their cars to cheat on emissions tests for years.

cues.zh: 这还没算上用户操作失误。
cues.en: And that’s before we include user error.

cues.zh: 在一次试用电子投票的苏格兰选举中，
cues.en: In one Scottish election, trialing electronic voting,

cues.zh: 一名观察员发现结果不合理后，结果得到了更正，
cues.en: a result was corrected after one observer noticed it didn’t make sense,

cues.zh: 并在最后一刻阻止了公布。
cues.en: and stopped the announcement at the last minute.

cues.zh: 原来有人忘了一直向右滚动
cues.en: Turns out that someone forgot to scroll all the way to the right

cues.zh: 去读取含结果的 Excel 电子表格中的列。
cues.en: to read the columns on an Excel spreadsheet with the results in.

cues.zh: 即使你无法攻破选举，你仍然可以破坏信任。
cues.en: And even if you can’t compromise the election, you can still break trust.

cues.zh: 你仍然可以让人怀疑投票机，或整个计票系统，
cues.en: You can still cast doubt on a voting machine, or the entire counting system,

cues.zh: 只需在机器里留下一个未知的 U 盘，拍张照，发到网上。
cues.en: just by leaving an unknown USB drive in it, taking a picture, and posting it online.

cues.zh: 或者干脆伪造一张这样的照片。
cues.en: Or just faking a photo of that.

cues.zh: 要破坏电子选举，你其实不需要真的攻破它：
cues.en: To break an electronic election, you don’t actually need to break it:

cues.zh: 你只需要对结果制造足够的怀疑。
cues.en: you just need to cast enough doubt on the result.

cues.zh: 用纸质选票和实体投票箱，要做到这一点难得多。
cues.en: It is a lot more difficult to do that with paper and physical ballot boxes.

cues.zh: 而这一切还没说到那个真正糟糕的主意：
cues.en: And all this is before we get to the really terrible idea:

cues.zh: 让人们能用手机或电脑在家投票。
cues.en: that people should be able to use their phone or computer to vote from home.

cues.zh: 现在，我确信你个人正在观看此内容的设备
cues.en: Now, I’m sure the device that you, personally, are watching this on

cues.zh: 没有恶意软件，而且是最新的。当然是啦。
cues.en: is malware-free and up-to-date. Of course it is.

cues.zh: 但你能对你家里的每个人都放心吗？
cues.en: But can you trust that for everyone in your family?

cues.zh: 对你同一条街上的每个人呢？
cues.en: For everyone on your street?

cues.zh: 具体数字会因你采用哪家安全公司的数据而不同，
cues.en: The exact numbers differ depending on which security firm’s figures you go with,

cues.zh: 但可以肯定，大量电脑
cues.en: but it's safe to say that a huge number of computers

cues.zh: 都感染了某种恶意软件。
cues.en: are infected with some sort of malware.

cues.zh: 大量手机仍运行着老旧、存在漏洞的操作系统版本。
cues.en: Huge numbers of phones are on old, vulnerable versions of their operating systems.

cues.zh: 而这还只是诈骗分子搭建僵尸网络、搞点小勒索。
cues.en: And that’s just scammers setting up botnets and minor extortions.

cues.zh: 想象一下，能组织起的那种攻击
cues.en: Imagine the sort of attack that could be put together

cues.zh: 由一支有国家政府支持、资金充足的小团队发起。
cues.en: by a small, well-funded team backed by a national government.

cues.zh: 这种攻击的扩展性会非常、非常强。
cues.en: That sort of attack would scale very, very well.

cues.zh: 找到系统中的一个漏洞，然后突然之间
cues.en: Find the one hole in the system, and suddenly

cues.zh: 改变一张选票和篡改数百万张选票的成本几乎一样：
cues.en: it costs roughly the same to change one vote as it does to alter millions:

cues.zh: 而你的阴谋团队可以保持得非常、非常小。
cues.en: and your conspiracy stays very, very small indeed.

cues.zh: 也许你甚至不用踏入那个你正在黑客攻击其选举的国家。
cues.en: Maybe you don’t even have to set foot in the country whose elections you’re hacking.

cues.zh: 对此，我常会听到几种反对意见。
cues.en: Now, there are a couple of regular objections I get to this.
